title: Kubernetes cluster health
description: A cluster where pods are born and die continuously: 120 pod identities an hour with a 30-minute mean lifetime. Entity identity is ephemeral by design, so silence is meaningless without knowing whether the entity was supposed to still exist. The catalog targets 4,000 births per hour; this spec runs 120 per hour so a single-machine run stays usable while keeping the retirement behaviour — the capability most stream processors discover they lack — fully exercised.
stresses: Entity identity is ephemeral by design, so silence is meaningless without knowing whether the entity was supposed to still exist: a pod that stops reporting was probably scaled down on purpose. A consumer holding durable per-entity state with a wake schedule accumulates orphaned states and absence alarms against entities that were correctly deleted. Entity retirement is the concept most designs discover they lack.

state.name: resource_usage_true
state.description: True CPU/memory composite utilisation of the pod. Diurnal workload curve; dropped to near zero when the pod is evicted or its metrics path is severed.

state.name: restarts_true
state.description: True cumulative restart count of the pod. Steps up in bursts under crash_loop; a counter whose rate is the diagnosis and whose absolute value means nothing across pods.

state.name: pod_phase
state.description: Whether the pod is scheduled and running. No free dynamics: stepped to zero by evictions and drains. The trigger for the event-driven status channel.

state.name: net_health
state.description: Whether the pod's network path is intact. No free dynamics: stepped to zero by network_partition. The root of the metric-silence signature.

state.name: config_bias
state.description: Hidden staleness of the pod's declared resource limits. Corrupts the resource_usage channel through its observation_bias: reads up to 20 points high while the pod is actually healthy.

channels.name: resource_usage
channels.description: The pod metrics sample. Stops moving when the pod dies or its metrics path is severed, which is exactly why a consumer must know whether the entity is supposed to exist.

faults.description: The pod is evicted under node pressure: phase drops and the metrics reading collapses to near zero. Looks exactly like a pod that was correctly deleted — the consumer that cannot tell the difference has no defence here.
The pod thrashes against its memory limit in pulses: usage spikes repeatedly and settles. Sustained, not a single event — a cooldown-aware consumer absorbs it, a naive one fights it.

The pod's network path is severed: metrics stop flowing and the resource reading freezes low. The heartbeat continues from the out-of-band agent, so only the absent metric stream betrays the partition — silence with a known cause.
The pod's container crashes on startup and the restart counter climbs in bursts. The rate of the counter is the signal; its absolute level is meaningless across pods.

A scheduled node drain evicts pods legitimately: the pod is terminated because it was supposed to be, and the metrics reading collapses exactly as under pod_eviction. The false-positive trap — same signature, different truth.

The pod runs against stale resource limits: the metric reads up to 20 points high while the pod is actually healthy. Only the divergence from the sibling pods and the pod's own history betrays it — the instrument-lying label of this domain.

effectors.name: evict_pod
effectors.description: Force-evict the pod so it is rescheduled elsewhere. High-risk, high-cost: the remedy for a crashing or lying pod, and expensive when the call was wrong.

effectors.name: scale_replicas
effectors.description: Raise the replica count of the deployment backing the pod: load spreads and the observed usage falls as siblings take the work.

effectors.name: cordon_node
effectors.description: Mark the node unschedulable so no new work lands on the partitioned path. Contains the blast radius; does not claim to fix the partition itself.

profiles.name: nominal
profiles.description: A base fleet of eight pods under continuous churn, one fault per scenario, 24-hour traces.

profiles.name: correlated_cascade
profiles.description: A control-plane event flips many pods into crash-loop at once: eight restart counters climbing together. The alarm-flood case, and the one where per-entity restart-rate triggers each open their own episode.

profiles.name: sensor_pathology
profiles.description: Weighted toward the lies: the stale-limit reading and the frozen metrics, with the legitimately-evicted pod as control. The labels a fixed threshold on resource usage cannot separate.
